claims.text: Cast Co-Cr-Fe-Ni- or Ti-Zr-Nb-based multi-principal element alloys can have limited ductility, coarse grains above 10 μm, and susceptibility to brittle intermetallic formation during standard heat treatment.
Combined carbon and oxygen doping, severe plastic deformation, and short-duration annealing can produce a sub-50 nm FCC+HCP solid solution without brittle intermetallics.
Introducing 0.5–1.0 at.% carbon and 1.0–3.0 at.% oxygen by ball milling or sputtering will form a massive interstitial solid-solution precursor.
High-pressure torsion or high-energy ball milling will reduce the alloy grain size below 50 nm.
Annealing at 900 °C for 3 minutes can stabilize an FCC+HCP dual-phase structure while avoiding grain coarsening and carbide or oxide precipitation.
A high-purity argon or vacuum atmosphere prevents uncontrolled oxidation during processing.
Ordered oxygen complexes act as pinning centers for both dislocations and grain boundaries.
Carbon-modulated stacking-fault energy stabilizes metastable FCC/HCP interfaces and promotes nanotwinning.
Oxygen-derived ordered complexes suppress grain growth during annealing and promote wavy slip that enhances ductility.
Carbon increases stacking-fault energy, stabilizing the FCC matrix against excessive martensitic transformation while permitting a controlled HCP fraction.
The combination of ordered-oxygen-complex pinning and carbon-induced phase stability prevents Laves or M23C6 nucleation by retaining a metastable solid solution.
A grain size below 50 nm provides grain-boundary strengthening.
The proposed material will have yield strength above 800 MPa, tensile strength above 1200 MPa, and elongation above 20%.
The final microstructure will contain no observable Laves or M23C6 phase.
Oxygen contents above 3.0 at.% cause grain-boundary segregation and brittle intergranular fracture.
Carbon contents above the solid-solubility limit cause M23C6 or molybdenum-carbide precipitation.
Longer annealing permits grain coarsening beyond 50 nm or decomposition into brittle intermetallics.

The oxygen threshold separating ordered-oxygen-complex formation from grain-boundary segregation is not established for Co-Cr-Fe-Ni and other proposed systems because the cited ordered-complex evidence concerns Ti-Zr-Nb alloys.
The stability of the proposed dual-phase nanostructure under deformation at an equivalent strain rate of 10^3 s^-1 is not quantified by the cited studies.

contradictions.description: The operative route specifies a 900 °C, 3-minute anneal and identifies excessive annealing as an instability boundary, but one falsification rule treats failure after SPS at 1100 °C for 10 minutes as falsifying the short-anneal hypothesis. That sample lies outside the stated processing window, so its failure would not contradict the hypothesis.

The stated baseline is a conventionally hot-rolled and annealed alloy or a carbon-only alloy, whereas the experiment does not include either control and instead compares two differently consolidated or annealed interstitial-doped samples.
